subject: Req/Resp spec, auth and routing follow-up — Starglass integration
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Chen <alex.chen@starglass.io>, Sara Kumar <sara.k@starglass.io>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 8 Nov 2027 09:21:00 -0800
Subject: Quick recap + integration questions (SDK auth, routing, req/resp semantics)

Hi Alex / Sara —

Thanks again for the demo this morning — excited about the potential to cut inference costs for your triage workflows. As promised, a short recap plus a few technical clarifications we need to lock in before a scoped POC.

Recap / next steps:
- POC target: ingest 200k triage messages/week, ~1.5s latency p50 target for single-turn summaries, batch reranking for top-3 suggestions.
- Timeline: kickoff week of Nov 22; 4-week POC with dashboarding and eval prompts.
- Primary success criteria: p50 latency < 2s, RU cost < $0.002 per message, and top-3 reranker precision >= 78% on your blind set.

Open technical clarifications (please confirm):
1) SDK & auth: do you want us to use your existing SSO/KMS, or is a token-based API key (Redwood-managed) acceptable for the POC? If token, what rotation cadence?
2) Routing: you mentioned two regions (US East + EU). For POC we'll route by region header and have fallback to a lower-cost variant — need confirmation on region breakdown and whether data residency is required.
3) Structured output / tool-calling: Will you require structured JSON from the model (fields: intent, urgency, suggested_action), or will free-text be acceptable initially? If structured, we should enable strict schema enforcement in the SDK (we can provide a validation hook).
4) Reranker vs embeddings: Are you planning to store dense embeddings in your vector DB (we support Faiss/Pinecone) and call a separate reranker, or do you want a single-pass reranker during retrieval?
5) Req/resp semantics: stop tokens, max_tokens, and streaming — do you rely on streaming partial tokens for your UI? If so, we need to coordinate how finalization is signaled (stream close vs final metadata).

I've attached a quick architecture sketch and a proposed mutual action plan. Looping in Laura (infra) to comment on the SDK/auth side.

Thanks,
Ben

ben.carter@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0132

Date: Mon, 8 Nov 2027 11:02:00 -0800

Thanks Ben — great summary. Quick answers inline: 

1) SDK & auth: For the POC, token-based API keys are fine. We'll rotate keys every 30 days and can provide a service account with IP allowlist. POC tokens can be passed via Authorization: Bearer <token>. For production we'll want KMS/HSM integration.

2) Routing: POC traffic will originate from US East only. Production may include EU later, but not in the POC scope. Data residency: not yet required for POC.

3) Structured output: We prefer structured JSON for the suggested_action and urgency fields — helps downstream systems. Intent can be free-text initially. Please include a validator.

4) Reranker vs embeddings: We'll store dense vectors in our vector DB and call a separate reranker after retrieval. Latency budget per rerank call is ~300ms.

5) Streaming: Our UI prefers streaming for progressive display, but can handle finalization via a terminal metadata message (e.g., {"status":"done"}). If streaming is enabled, please ensure partial results include token offsets so we can stitch with highlights.

A couple of follow-ups: do you have a sample request/response schema for chat vs completions, and can you confirm tokenization differences (how max_tokens applies to chat role/content framing)?

Appreciate it — Alex
Alex Chen | Senior PM, Integrations — Starglass Health

Subject: Re: Quick recap + integration questions (SDK auth, routing, req/resp semantics)

Hi all — thanks Ben for the loop. I pulled together concise examples and notes below. Attaching a text file with SDK auth snippets as well (redwood-sdk-auth-snippets.txt).

1) SDK & auth (POC):
- Use Authorization: Bearer <api_key>. If you need IP allowlist, we can accept it at the account level. For production we support customer-managed KMS + key-wrapping; we'll exchange a signed cert for mutual TLS when you are ready.
- Rotation: 30 days is fine. For automated rotation we can support a short-lived token flow (OAuth client_credentials) that hits your identity provider — we have a plug-in for common IdPs.

2) Request/response schemas — chat vs completions
- Chat (recommended for dialog and streaming progress): request uses roles and messages array, e.g.
  {
  "model": "redwood-chat-3b",
  "messages": [ {"role":"system","content":"You are a summarizer."}, {"role":"user","content":"Summarize..."} ],
  "max_tokens": 256,
  "stop": ["\nEND\n"],
  "stream": true
  }

  Response (streaming): a sequence of delta events that include a "type" (token|metadata), incremental "text" and optional "token_index". Final message includes {"type":"metadata","status":"done","usage":{"prompt_tokens":45,"completion_tokens":120}}.

- Completions (simpler single-turn, less structured): request payload is prompt + max_tokens; good for single-shot templates.

Tokenization note:
- Token counting is applied to the entire serialized request (roles + content) for chat. So when you set max_tokens=256, that is the generation allowance on top of the request tokens; total tokens billed = prompt_tokens + completion_tokens. The SDK exposes a token_count helper to estimate before sending.

3) Structured output / validation
- For strict JSON outputs we recommend the SDK "schema" field that accepts a JSON Schema or a simplified shape. The runtime runs a validation step and returns either the parsed object or a validation error with the raw text so you can fall back. Example response body (final metadata):
  {"intent":"escalate","urgency":"high","suggested_action":{"type":"open_ticket","queue":"clinical-review"}}

- If you prefer permissive, use a post-hoc validator on your side and mark the model's output as "candidate" rather than canonical.

4) Embeddings + reranker pattern
- Recommended: store 512-d dense vectors in your vector DB, retrieve top-50, then call a lightweight reranker model (redwood-rerank-sm) that scores candidates. That keeps most latency in the vector DB retrieval (typically <100ms for Faiss), then reranker <250ms. For your 300ms budget we recommend: Faiss tuned for HNSW + 8-16 probes, and a batch rerank call with a 128-token context.

5) Streaming semantics + offsets
- Streaming events include token_index and cumulative char_offset. We close the stream with a metadata event {"status":"done","final":true}. Partial results may include low-confidence corrections; we include a confidence score per token if requested.

6) Stop tokens / max_tokens best practices
- Use explicit stop tokens when you need strict termination. For chat-based structured JSON, we wrap the JSON in a code fence and use a stop of ["```", "\nEND\n"] to avoid accidental continuation.
- Set max_tokens conservatively for POC (e.g., 256) and use the SDK token estimator in your UI to prevent truncation.

7) Examples (high level)
- Chat streaming (progressive): preferred for summaries with UI streaming.
- Completions: preferred for short templated fills where you don't need role framing.

Karthik / infra note on reranker scale: if you plan to do synchronous reranking at 300ms SLA, we should size Dedicated pool with a low-latency model (int8) and add a hot cache for top-k candidates. Happy to size this into the M.A.P.

If this looks good I'll drop the schema snippets into the shared Drive link and Ben can push the M.A.P. to your procurement folks.

Cheers,

Quick infra note from my side — adding for completeness:
- For the POC we'll provision a small Dedicated pool (1-2 GPUs with quantized endpoints) to keep latency predictable for reranker calls.
- We'll enable automatic prefix caching for repeated triage templates; this will reduce per-message prompt tokens and cost.
- Regarding streaming: SDK exposes a websocket and an HTTP chunked stream. The websocket provides lower overhead and explicit token_index events; recommend websocket for the UI streaming path.

I'll coordinate an infra sizing call next week if you want exact CPU/GPU numbers.

-Karthik
